Requirement Analysis:
We must ship a Python 3.10 repository for Excel-like data processing with a strict, acyclic import architecture and a canonical API. Protocol-level files are fixed: requirements.txt (lists pytest only), Main.py (thin entrypoint exposing run_demo()->dict and printing at most one result under __name__), and tests/test_main.py (the only test file, with exactly three concise pytest tests). The package excel_processor contains exactly: model.py (sole owner of Cell, Row, Sheet and imports no project modules), operations.py, csv_io.py, report.py (these three may import only from .model), and __init__.py (re-exports only: Cell, Row, Sheet, filter_rows, sort_rows, aggregate_column, loads_csv, dumps_csv, build_report). Import direction is one-way: model <- {operations, csv_io, report} <- __init__ <- {Main, tests}. No reverse edges, no TYPE_CHECKING hacks that break acyclicity. Full API specification:
- excel_processor.model.Cell(value: object | None = None): mutable value attribute, no cross-module imports.
- excel_processor.model.Row(cells: list[Cell]): defensively copies input cells; values() -> list[object] returns a list of the contained Cell.value.
- excel_processor.model.Sheet(rows: list[Row]): defensively copies; classmethod from_values(values: list[list[object]]) -> Sheet rejects ragged non-empty rows (all non-empty rows must have same length); to_values() -> list[list[object]] returns snapshot of values; row_count() -> int; column_count() -> int; get_cell(row: int, column: int) -> Cell; set_cell(row: int, column: int, value: object) -> None. All indexed methods reject negative or out-of-range indices with IndexError.
- excel_processor.operations.filter_rows(sheet: Sheet, predicate: Callable[[Row], bool]) -> Sheet: produces a new Sheet with deep-new Row/Cell objects for retained rows; input Sheet is not mutated.
- excel_processor.operations.sort_rows(sheet: Sheet, key: Callable[[Row], object], reverse: bool = False) -> Sheet: returns a new Sheet sorted by key; stable; deep-new objects; does not mutate input.
- excel_processor.operations.aggregate_column(sheet: Sheet, column: int) -> dict[str, object]: validates column index; scans rows to compute: count (int, total rows), missing (int, count of None or empty string in target column), numeric_count (int, count of numeric values excluding bool), sum (numeric sum over numeric values, 0 if none), min (numeric min or None if none), max (numeric max or None if none).
- excel_processor.csv_io.loads_csv(text: str) -> Sheet: parses CSV from the given string using csv and io.StringIO only; cells are strings; empty cells remain ""; ragged non-empty rows raise ValueError; no filesystem access.
- excel_processor.csv_io.dumps_csv(sheet: Sheet) -> str: serializes Sheet values to CSV string using csv and io.StringIO; string-preserving semantics; no filesystem.
- excel_processor.report.build_report(sheet: Sheet) -> dict[str, object]: returns {row_count, column_count, missing_cells} where missing counts cells that are None or "".
- excel_processor.__init__ re-exports exactly: Cell, Row, Sheet, filter_rows, sort_rows, aggregate_column, loads_csv, dumps_csv, build_report.
Main wiring and tests:
- Main.py must use `from excel_processor import Sheet, filter_rows, sort_rows, aggregate_column, build_report` only; provide run_demo()->dict that constructs a small in-memory Sheet, performs filter/sort/aggregate/report deterministically, and returns a dict result. Under __name__ guard, print at most one result.
- tests/test_main.py must have exactly three tests: (1) run_demo returns a dict; (2) operations on the literal fixtures using the specified predicate and data yield exact expected results (filter keeps [[3,"c"],[2,"b"]]; sorting [[3],[1],[2]] ascending yields [[1],[2],[3]]; aggregate on the four-row sheet yields count=4, missing=1, numeric_count=3, sum=6, min=1, max=3); (3) CSV round-trip based on loads_csv("name,value\nA,1\nB,\n") yields the exact matrix and build_report returns row_count=3, column_count=2, missing_cells=1.
These constraints enforce deterministic, headless tests and a clean separation of domain logic from runtime concerns.

As an analyst, I want to sort rows by a column-derived key to inspect ordered results.
As a report consumer, I want to aggregate a numeric column to see counts, sum, min, and max with missing values handled properly.
As a developer, I want to load and dump CSV data to exchange sheets with other tools.
As a tester, I want a deterministic demo and concise tests that validate core APIs.
